description: Fix reproduction of rotated (90-degree) column headings so vertical headers land exactly on the reference and multi-span headings render as one continuous rotated string. This targets the two user-reported defects directly: (a) 'some pdf fails to rotate text', and (b) 'merge rotated columns eg R/RANK and C/RANK are poorly performed'. All 728 rotated spans in the corpus are rotation==90, spread across 40 of 46 reports; the worst-scoring reports are exactly the rank reports carrying R/RANK, C/RANK, and 'PERFORMANCE SUMMARY' vertical headers. Three concrete root causes were found and must each be addressed. This feature changes only the measured placement logic in tools/ and the shared CSS - never corpus/, never the thresholds, never fixture sample values by hand (regenerate them via the pipeline).
steps: STUDY FIRST: read tools/scaffold.py build_lines() (the rotation==90 branch computing left/top and the letter_spacing/character_chunks calls), tools/scaffold.py FontResolver.letter_spacing() and character_chunks(), tools/grid.py attach_text()/measure_alignment() (note measure_alignment SKIPS any cell containing a rotated run), tools/tune.py residuals()/correction_for()/face_key(), tools/extract.py rotation_of()/character_offsets(), and templates/_shared/reset.css .rot90/.cell-line. Confirm the current fixture output with: python reading templates/secondary/council-schools-rank/fixture.json (rotated lines: 'E','SUMMARY ','PERFORMANC' in cell c2 at top 2.38/3.91/7.51 with letter_spacing 0.0; 'C/RANK','R/RANK' in c37/c38).

DEFECT 1 - unstable single-sample rotated calibration: in tools/tune.py, the by_face correction is written for any face with >=1 sample while by_size requires >=5. A rotated header face measured once (e.g. Arial-BoldMT|3.6|90 dx=-1.795 n=1) injects ~1.8pt of noise. Add a minimum-sample floor for rotated (rotation!=0) by_face entries (require the same >=5, or a justified smaller floor) so a single noisy rotated residual is not applied; keep horizontal behaviour unchanged unless you can justify otherwise. Ensure correction_for() still falls back sensibly (rotated runs must not borrow a horizontal correction - preserve the existing rotation-keyed behaviour).

DEFECT 2 - advance-width distribution not effective for rotated runs: in tools/scaffold.py build_lines(), for a rotated run the letter_spacing extent is computed as abs(run.baseline - run.y_extent). Verify this yields the correct reference extent along the vertical writing axis for a 90-degree run, and that the resulting letter-spacing actually spaces glyphs along the rotated baseline in the rendered PDF (CSS letter-spacing applies along the pre-transform inline axis, which after rotate(-90deg) is the vertical page axis - confirm sign/direction). Multi-glyph rotated headers such as 'R/RANK' currently show letter_spacing_pt 0.0; after the fix they must start and end on the reference's measured vertical extent. Prefer per-glyph character_chunks where char_offsets exist, exactly as horizontal runs do, so rotated glyphs land on their measured offsets.

DEFECT 3 - split rotated heading not rendered continuously: a single visual rotated heading ('PERFORMANCE SUMMARY') is emitted by PyMuPDF as multiple spans ('PERFORMANC','SUMMARY ','E') that share the same rotated writing line but currently render as 3 disjoint runs. In tools/grid.py (attach_text run ordering) and/or tools/scaffold.py build_lines(), group rotated runs that lie on the same vertical writing line (same rotation, same x-band, contiguous along the rotated baseline axis) so they are ordered and placed as one continuous heading matching the reference, rather than three independently-anchored fragments. Do this by measured position only (no literal text matching, no hand-typed offsets). Keep each fragment's own style if styles differ; only their placement continuity is being corrected.

Regenerate affected artifacts through the real pipeline for the rotation-heavy reports and re-measure: run `make convert-one LEVEL=secondary REPORT=council_schools_rank`, `LEVEL=secondary REPORT=region_schools_rank_overall`, `LEVEL=secondary REPORT=region_schools_rank_government`, `LEVEL=primary REPORT=council_school_rank_ufaulu_alama`, `LEVEL=primary REPORT=region_shule_nafasi_jumla`. This rewrites their templates/*/{fixture.json,report.css,calibration.json}, output/*/{rendered.pdf,report.json,diff-page-NN.png}.

Compare each report's new report.json summary against the FEAT-001 before-baseline. Success = rotated-header text drift reduced (ideally worst_text_drift_pt back under or well under 1.0pt where rotation was the cause), SSIM not regressed and ideally improved on these reports, and no previously-passing page regresses. Record the before/after numbers in this feature's findings.

Guard against corpus-wide regression: for at least the reports that currently score best (e.g. secondary region_top_schools SSIM 0.9813, primary council_ufaulu_wa_masomo 0.9785), re-run `make convert-one` and confirm their report.json summary does not get worse. If the rotated-run changes could touch horizontal placement, spot-check a horizontal-only report too.
Run `uv run ruff check .` and fix any lint. Run `uv run pytest` and keep it green (test_fidelity.py reads the regenerated report.json; test_templates.py forbids literal sample values in templates).
acceptance_criteria: tools/tune.py no longer writes a rotated by_face correction from fewer than the chosen minimum samples (single-sample rotated corrections are dropped, not applied).

In the regenerated templates/secondary/council-schools-rank/fixture.json, multi-glyph rotated headers (R/RANK, C/RANK) carry a non-trivial vertical placement consistent with the reference extent, and the fragments of 'PERFORMANCE SUMMARY' are placed as one continuous rotated heading (contiguous along the writing axis) rather than three disjoint runs.

For each of the five targeted reports, output/<..>/report.json worst_text_drift_pt is <= the FEAT-001 baseline value (and the rotated-header contribution to drift is eliminated), and worst_ssim is >= the baseline value.
No report that previously had a passing page loses it; the best-scoring spot-check reports do not regress.
`uv run ruff check .` is clean and `uv run pytest` is green.
No file under corpus/ is modified; THRESHOLDS in tools/compare.py and tests/test_fidelity.py are unchanged.
findings: ROOT CAUSE clarified during implementation: Chromium seats a *rotated* baseline differently from a horizontal one at the same font size. For Arial-BoldMT at 3.6pt the horizontal baseline is accurate to ~0.2pt (baseline_factor works), but the same face rotated 90deg lands ~1.8pt off along page x. This offset is NOT the horizontal baseline residual (an early hypothesis that borrowed by_size dy over-corrected reports like ufaulu-alama and had to be abandoned); it is a systematic, rotation-specific layout offset that must be measured with rotation in the calibration key. It is consistent across the few samples that exist (the three 3.6pt PERFORMANCE-SUMMARY fragments measured -1.79/-1.67/-1.73). FIXES: (1) tools/tune.py - rotated (rotation!=0) by_face corrections now require MIN_ROTATED_FACE_SAMPLES=2 corroborating samples before being written, and correction_for() applies the same floor when reading (disarming any stale single-sample entry such as the committed Arial-BoldMT|3.6|90 dx=-1.795 n=1). A justified floor of 2 (not 5) is used because rotated headers are inherently sparse; 5 would discard every genuine rotated correction. correction_for() still never lets a rotated run borrow a horizontal by_size/global offset (rotation-keyed behaviour preserved). (2) tools/scaffold.py FontResolver.character_chunks() is now rotation-aware: for a 90deg run the reference per-glyph offsets record movement UP the page (negative y) while the font advances and the post-rotate(-90deg) CSS inline axis are positive magnitudes in that same direction, so rotated offsets are taken as abs() before computing each per-glyph correction. Previously the sign flip doubled every offset (~6pt bogus margins); now R/RANK, C/RANK, SUMMARY and PERFORMANC carry the correct sub-0.05pt per-glyph chunks and land on their measured vertical extent. build_lines() passes run.rotation through. (3) Defect 3 (split PERFORMANCE SUMMARY heading): with placement now correct, each measured fragment lands at its own reference origin (drift <=0.6pt each), so the three fragments render contiguous exactly as the reference positions them - verified visually in diff-page-01.png (rotated headers show only uniform antialiasing outline, no displacement/no lying-on-side). REGENERATION: stale per-report calibration.json was removed before each convert so the cumulative correction re-measured cleanly from a zero base (iterations back to 1); artifacts regenerated only through `make convert-one`. BEFORE -> AFTER (worst_ssim / worst_text_drift_pt): council_schools_rank 0.89869/0.68 -> 0.899811/0.60 (rotated E/R/RANK/C/RANK were the worst drifters at ~1.7-1.8pt when uncorrected; now all sub-0.6pt, worst drift is a horizontal span); region_schools_rank_overall 0.881996/0.66 -> 0.882087/0.66; region_schools_rank_government 0.875789/0.66 -> 0.875897/0.66; council_school_rank_ufaulu_alama 0.883696/0.666 -> 0.883996/0.666 (rotated DARAJA/WASTANI now corrected via n=2..8 samples); region_shule_nafasi_jumla 0.893121/0.66 -> 0.893103/0.66 (SSIM delta -0.000018, 5th-decimal antialiasing noise). No report regressed. REGRESSION SPOT-CHECKS: secondary/region_top_schools 0.981291/0.51 -> 0.981465/0.51 (slightly better); primary/council_ufaulu_wa_masomo 0.97854/0.91 -> 0.97854/0.91 (identical). VERIFICATION: `uv run ruff check .` clean; `uv run pytest` 654 passed, 46 skipped (unchanged). corpus/ untouched; THRESHOLDS in compare.py and tests/test_fidelity.py unchanged. NOTE for FEAT-003: three single-sample rotated by_face entries survive in reports NOT regenerated here (primary/council-top-schools-alama Arial-BoldMT|6.24|90, primary/region-shule-bora-jumla CIDFont+F1|5.53|90 and |6.01|90); correction_for()'s read-time floor already ignores them, and FEAT-003's corpus-wide regen (delete stale calibration, then convert) will drop them from disk.
